lessons.key: weak_test::when a check s one line claim bundles multiple http status codes for one endpoint cite one test per status code one check per branch instead of a single proof a single proof only covers the branch its named test exercises
lessons.text: When a check's one-line claim bundles multiple HTTP status codes for one endpoint, cite one test per status code (one check per branch) instead of a single proof - a single proof only covers the branch its named test exercises.

lessons.key: ac_gap::a uniqueness rule stated as case insensitive in the spec s edge cases often also implies whitespace insensitive trim before comparing and before persisting write that test explicitly it is easy to miss
lessons.text: A uniqueness rule stated as case-insensitive in the spec's Edge Cases often also implies whitespace-insensitive (trim before comparing and before persisting) - write that test explicitly, it is easy to miss.

lessons.key: ac_gap::a business rule enforced only by the dto s bean validation e g min max is not enforced for callers that reach the service directly duplicate range bound checks at the service layer too not just at the controller boundary
lessons.text: A business rule enforced only by the DTO's bean validation (e.g. @Min/@Max) is not enforced for callers that reach the service directly - duplicate range/bound checks at the service layer too, not just at the controller boundary.

lessons.key: ac_gap::when a field is trimmed before persistence apply length size bean validation size to the trimmed value not the raw request value e g trim in the dto s constructor before validation runs not only in the service layer
lessons.text: When a field is trimmed before persistence, apply length/size bean-validation (@Size) to the trimmed value, not the raw request value - e.g. trim in the DTO's constructor before validation runs, not only in the service layer.

lessons.key: weak_test::a test proving a rejected write persisted nothing must assert the row count or absence of the record explicitly not just the http status code a 404 400 status alone does not prove nothing was written
lessons.text: A test proving a rejected write 'persisted nothing' must assert the row count (or absence of the record) explicitly, not just the HTTP status code - a 404/400 status alone does not prove nothing was written.
